_comment: Curated alarm-name -> citation registry read by scripts/check_alarm_citations.py (#1959). Every CloudWatch alarm that has been in ALARM >72h must have an entry here (exact AlarmName key) naming the incident row or issue that explains it, or the /wrap gate flags it by name. Since #2912 the same holds for an alarm that FIRED AND CLEARED within the last 72h (episode start and end both in-window, read from describe-alarm-history) — a flap between wraps is invisible to current-state duration by construction, so it needs an entry or an explicit --decoded line just like a standing red. Add an entry the same session a new long-red alarm (or flap) is triaged; remove/replace one once the underlying issue closes AND the alarm has actually cleared live. Since #2996 a citation that names a `#N` must name an issue that is still OPEN: the gate reads `gh issue view` for every currently-lit alarm's citation and flags a dead reference, because a citation string is not an owner (measured 2026-08-22: 4 of 7 entries pointed at closed issues, 3 of them on lit alarms). A citation with NO `#N` is never flagged by that check — a dated, self-clearing state is honestly cited in prose — but the 14-day `issueless_ancient_reds` rule still forces a `#N` past that tenure. PRUNE an entry when its alarm recovers. Since #3258 a citation may not assert a recurrence NEGATIVE ("no recurrence since", "has not recurred") unless the same note names how it was derived — the log group it was read from, or the query that read it (filter-log-events / describe-alarm-history / start-query). A recurrence-negative is unfalsifiable from the registry alone, and the measured instance hid a live recurrence for four days: this alarm's entry read "fixed by #3066/PR#3075 …, no recurrence since" while the identical finding fingerprint 539c6d sat in /aws/lambda/life-platform-qa-smoke inside the last 72h. Enforced offline against the committed file by tests/test_check_alarm_citations.py::test_the_live_registry_carries_no_underived_recurrence_negative (scripts/check_alarm_citations.py::unfalsifiable_negatives), so it runs on every PR rather than only at wrap. A POSITIVE claim needs no marker — it is checkable by looking.

ai-canary-overall.citation: #3413 — POST /api/board_ask returns 504 to real readers. The canary's Monday 2026-08-31 run caught it ('board_grounded:status: no response (transport failure)', Sandbox.Timedout after 30.00s) and the alarm has been lit since 09:22 PT that day. REGRESSION, not a standing state: this alarm was OK from 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-31, 28 days green. Cause measured: board_quality_gate's QG_INVOKE_TIMEOUT_S caps the coach-quality-gate invoke at 10s while that lambda's AWS/Lambda Duration Maximum has been 11.5-17s EVERY day since at least 08-24, so the invoke is guaranteed to time out and burn ~11.4s of a 30s reader budget for a result that is then discarded (fail-open). Expiry: this clears on a subsequent canary run (Mon/Wed/Fri 16:20 UTC) once #3413 ships. PRUNE this entry once the alarm has been OK longer than the 72h flap window.
ai-canary-overall.note: Added 2026-09-01 (Session Q), while the alarm was still ~31h old and therefore BELOW the 72h citation bar — the gate was silent on it and would have stayed silent until 2026-09-03. Cited early on purpose: this is the #1959 'a new red hiding among the old ones' case, and it was a live public-surface regression across the launch itself. The 72h bar is a floor for when a citation becomes MANDATORY, not advice to wait. Found by reading the alarm board rather than by any gate escalating it.

ai-tokens-daily-brief-runaway.note: FLAP, not a standing red (#2912 detector). Entered ALARM at 2026-09-04 09:45 PT and again 10:09 PT, each clearing within a minute (describe-alarm-history, 4 transitions). Cause, from the LifePlatform/AI AnthropicOutputTokens{daily-brief} series: the 2026-09-03 Saturday re-anchor forced a brief regeneration at 20:00 PT (8,971 tokens) on top of that day's 10:00 PT send (13,566), and the 09-04 send (8,384 + 11,585) then sat inside the same trailing 86400s Sum window — 30,000-token threshold crossed transiently as the window slid, cleared as the 09-03 10:00 datapoint aged out. No defect: two brief runs in one day is the reset's designed behaviour, and the 09-04 send alone (19,969) is under threshold. Prose citation deliberately carries no '#N' — nothing to fix; the dated self-clearing state is the sanctioned shape. RE-POINTED 2026-09-05 (#3505): the flap's MECHANISM — three ordinary runs summing inside one 86400s window on a reset day — is now structurally impossible rather than merely explained, because the alarm's period is one run's own window. The threshold was re-derived from n=71 hourly Sum datapoints over the trailing 35 days (median 4,717 · Q3 7,664 · max 31,970).

An operator's off-schedule {"dry_run": true} daily-brief invoke at 2026-08-30T15:55:39Z read the computed_metrics row 45 minutes before daily-metrics-compute's own cron(40 16 * * ? *) writes it, so the row was absent by construction and the ops metric went out at 1.0. compute-pipeline-stale.note: Added 2026-08-31 at the (e10) flap check (#2912); ROOT CAUSE ADDED 2026-09-02 (#3430). Derived, not remembered — three queries: (1) describe-alarm-history shows one OK->ALARM 2026-08-30T15:56:48Z on datapoint 1.0 @ 2026-08-29T15:56Z sampleCount 2, and one ALARM->OK 2026-08-31T15:56:48Z on 0.0 @ 2026-08-30T15:56Z sampleCount 1; (2) get-metric-statistics on LifePlatform::ComputePipelineStaleness{Source=computed_metrics} period 60 puts the 1.0 at 2026-08-30T15:55Z and a 0.0 at 17:00Z — two emissions inside the alarm's one rolling window; (3) /aws/lambda/daily-brief stream 2026/08/30/[$LATEST]76290f64dc2147f491b30f6339e39aee starts 15:55:39Z, first line '[daily-brief] DRY_RUN mode', then 'No pre-computed metrics for 2026-08-29 — computing inline (fallback)'. The exact-24h duration is alarm arithmetic (period 86400, EvaluationPeriods 1 => one evaluation tick per day at a fixed offset), not a 24h data gap. CLASS, derived from a 60-day get-metric-statistics sweep (the full retention of 5-minute data) rather than from memory: the metric emitted 1.0 exactly four times — 2026-07-26T16:05Z, 2026-07-26T16:10Z, 2026-07-27T16:35Z, 2026-08-30T15:55Z — all four before the 16:40Z compute cron, none of them the scheduled 17:00Z brief, and every scheduled run in that window emitted 0.0 (that sweep is also the derivation for the positive claim that the two cycle-11 genesis mornings #1962 was filed about were themselves off-schedule emissions, not scheduled reds). Fixed in daily_brief_lambda by _compute_staleness_observation_authoritative: a run that cannot answer the pipeline's question emits nothing. PRUNE this entry once the episode ages out of the 72h window (after 2026-09-03T15:57Z) and #3430 is closed.

life-platform-dlq-depth-warning.citation: #3829 — CAUSE RESOLVED, producer fixed; kept pointed here until the issue closes. Both siblings re-entered ALARM 2026-09-15T17:18Z over one message, {"cycle_date": "2026-09-15"}, SentTimestamp 1789492547367, produced by coach-ensemble-digest (its last log event is 1789492547247, 120ms earlier). That cycle ran 3 x 90,000ms Status:timeout and wrote no ENSEMBLE#digest/CYCLE#2026-09-15 row. TWO EARLIER READINGS ON THIS CITATION WERE WRONG AND ARE CORRECTED HERE. (1) 'Duration has crept 57-62s -> the ceiling over eight days' was an eight-day artifact: over 30 days it is a step function — median 1,326ms (08-15..08-30, n=16) to 62,279ms (08-31..09-14, n=15), 47x overnight, with no commit to the module. budget_guard pauses "ensemble" at tier >= 1 and SSM /life-platform/budget-tier dropped to 0 at 2026-08-31T17:00:12Z, minutes before that day's cron: the 90s ceiling had been sized while the feature was dark and returning a ~1.3s fallback. (2) The '2026-09-13 ran 52.4s with ONE invocation and still has no row' anomaly was an off-by-one in a period=86400 CloudWatch read — a daily bucket is labelled by its START in UTC and renders in local -07:00, so the 52.4s/n=1 datapoint is the 2026-09-14 run, which DOES have a row. Re-measured per day in explicit 17:00Z windows: 09-13 = 90,000ms x3 (no row), 09-14 = 52,382ms x1 (row), 09-15 = 90,000ms x3 (no row), 09-16 = 103,662ms x1 (row), 09-17 = 115,213ms x1 (row). Every missing row is a 3x-timeout day; there is no second, independent write failure. #3836 raised the ceiling 90 -> 300 (CDK-deployed 2026-09-16T04:07:27Z) and the queue has been empty with both alarms OK since 2026-09-15T21:07Z. Filed 2026-09-15; corrected and re-measured 2026-09-18.
life-platform-dlq-depth-warning.note: Sibling alarm; both point at #3829, which stays open for its residual acceptance rather than for a live failure. Do not re-cite as cured on a drained queue alone — the queue clearing is a different instant from the producer being fixed. What now covers the producer directly is the nightly qa-smoke check `ensemble_digest_liveness` (lambdas/operational/ensemble_digest_qa.py): it reports a missing ENSEMBLE#digest/CYCLE# row without anyone reading this queue, which is the coverage gap that let 09-13 and 09-15 sit unnoticed for eight days. This entry is the DEPTH alarm — it lights on the queue holding messages at all.

prediction-gradable-share-low.citation: deliberate arming transition (lit 2026-08-26), clearing by DILUTION rather than by the _retire_ungradeable mechanism its own CDK comment names — re-derive at the next wrap; issueless_ancient_reds forces a #N by 2026-09-09
prediction-gradable-share-low.note: ADDED 2026-08-28 (Session I). Lit 2026-08-26T10:25 PT; crosses the 72h bar 2026-08-29 ~10:25 PT, hence cited now. The alarm's own CDK comment (cdk/stacks/monitoring_prediction_alarms.py:65-73) says it 'fires on the CURRENT corpus the day it deploys (28/50 pending are legacy qualitative rows) and clears as the evaluator retires them at window end (_retire_ungradeable) — deliberate, same posture as #727'. The firing is therefore expected. WHAT IS NOT EXPECTED, and is why this note exists rather than a bare 'deliberate': measured LifePlatform/Predictions daily 2026-08-23..08-26, GradableShare rises 0.3951 / 0.4024 / 0.4024 / 0.4556 while UngradeablePendingCount is FLAT at 49 / 49 / 49 / 49. The share is improving because the GRADABLE numerator is growing, not because legacy rows are being retired. _retire_ungradeable only retires a record once its domain-clamped window has ELAPSED, so a flat 49 is consistent with 'no window has elapsed yet' AND with 'the retirement is not running' — this note does NOT claim to distinguish them, because I did not read the pending corpus out of DynamoDB. That is the open question. RE-DERIVE, do not trust this note: if UngradeablePendingCount is still exactly 49 at the next wrap, the stated clearing mechanism is not the one clearing it and this earns an issue. The 14-day issueless_ancient_reds rule forces a #N by 2026-09-09.

life-platform-canary-anthropic-failure.citation: #3830 — a FIRED-AND-CLEARED flap that is fully explained and is the root of tonight's fleet-rollback incident. ALARM 2026-09-15T19:55:44Z -> OK 20:10:44Z (15 min, one cycle). Cause: a single Bedrock `ServiceUnavailableException` — a vendor 503 — on the canary's `anthropic` check at 19:54:50Z, with DDB, S3, MCP and the subscribe flow all round-tripping clean in the same run. The alarm is CORRECT and needed no change: it fired on a real failed inference round-trip and cleared on the next clean one. What it exposed is that ONE datapoint had three consumers with three different confidences: the canary's own email path SUPPRESSED it as a first occurrence, this alarm fired and self-cleared, and the CI/CD smoke gate treated it as gating and auto-reverted 85 Lambdas (run 35013357326). Fixed by PR #3831, merged 28247778f and DEPLOYED 2026-09-16T01:26:13Z (verified in the deployed bundle): `LANE_EXTERNAL_TRANSIENT` + `lane_for_result` classify the FAILURE MODE, not just the check, so a vendor transient is counted in `failed_external_transient` and excluded from `failed_deploy_health` — the only key the smoke oracle gates on. A recurrence of THIS alarm is now expected to be non-gating; if a future 503 ever reverts a deploy again, that is a NEW finding, not this one.
life-platform-canary-anthropic-failure.note: Deliberately cited rather than suppressed, and the alarm is deliberately NOT retuned. A 15-minute flap on a real vendor outage is this alarm doing its job — it is the only instrument of the three that got the confidence level right, being loud without being destructive. #3830's remaining half (acceptance box 3) is retry-before-gate: making a SINGLE first-occurrence datapoint incapable of reverting a fleet, which is the property the canary's own email suppression already has and the deploy gate still does not. Until that lands, a SECOND transient inside one smoke window could still gate. Recorded 2026-09-16 by Session AF, the session that caused, diagnosed and fixed the episode in the same night.
